summary.intent: Execute Phase 36 (inline-upload-progress) using the GSD wave-based workflow, refactoring the upload store to per-file tracking and replacing the popup upload UI with inline progress indicators in the file browser.
summary.outcome: Both plans completed successfully across 2 waves. The upload Zustand store was refactored to Map-based per-file tracking, and a new UploadListItem component was built and wired into FileList. A React Rules of Hooks violation discovered during verification was fixed inline before phase completion.

repo: The upload store uses Zustand with a Map<string, PerFileUpload> structure after the refactor — per-file actions are addFile, updateFileProgress, setFileStatus, setFileComplete, removeFile, cancelFile, retryFile.
FileList uses virtual entry merging to show upload rows alongside real file entries, with folder-scoped filtering and alphabetical sort.
UploadModal and UploadItem components were deleted in favor of the inline UploadListItem approach — popup CSS removed, inline upload CSS added to upload.css.
useDropUpload drives the upload loop with independent cancel tokens per file; useFileUpload derives batch-level fields from the per-file Map for backward compatibility.
The worktree at /Users/michael/Code/cipher-box-wt-phase36 was a stale artifact from a previous session — safe to remove.

code.finding: Early return `if (!file) return null` was placed before three useCallback hooks (handleCancel, handleDismiss, handleRetry), causing a React Rules of Hooks violation when a file is removed from the store during the completion flash timer. All hooks must be declared before any conditional returns.

workflow: GSD wave executors run in isolated git worktrees and commit with --no-verify; orchestrator merges worktree branches back and runs pre-commit hooks post-wave.
STATE.md merge conflicts are expected when merging worktree branches — resolved by taking the agent's version.
The verifier catches React hook ordering violations that aren't caught by TypeScript or unit tests — useful safety net before phase completion.
Minor inline fixes found during verification can bypass the full gap-closure cycle (plan-phase --gaps → execute-phase --gaps-only) when the fix is trivial and well-understood.
